text:
marta: Heads up — after relabeling the holdout set for the new 2.7b reranker we see NDCG@10 drop ~3.2% and MRR down ~1.1% vs baseline on the same candidates :thinking:
devon: did we change query or doc formatting in the relabel pipeline?
sasha: we changed one thing: we started normalizing newline -> space and stripping trailing punctuation for docs (to match prod tokenizer).
alex: can you paste the eval command you ran?
marta: running the same eval harness as before, here's the command:
```
python eval_rerank.py --model rnk-2.7b-new --holdout path/to/holdout_relabel.jsonl --k 10 --metrics ndcg,mrr --batch 128
```
devon: can you share minimal sample from holdout_relabel.jsonl (one query + 3 candidates) so we can diff?
marta: sure, anonymized sample below:
```json
{"query": "how to reset password?", "candidates": ["Click Settings > Security.", "Reset via email link.", "Use admin console to set new pass!"]}
```
sasha: aha — note the exclamation in candidate 3 and periods in others. The pipeline strip/punct change will remove punctuation differences and collapse some candidate text; that can alter tokenization boundaries and attention patterns in small models.
alex: i suspect the relabel change changed truncation points — some docs lost a trailing sentence used as a strong relevance signal. Can we run a small A/B where we only apply newline->space and keep punctuation?
marta: done, quick run single shard (10k queries) — NDCG@10 delta is +0.5% vs fully relabeled, still -2.7% vs original holdout.
devon: send comparison of token lengths for candidates before/after relabel (histogram). Also run eval with quantized model (int8) vs float for the same holdout to rule quant noise.
sasha: quick quant check results:
float (fp16): NDCG@10 0.421
int8: NDCG@10 0.419
MRR fp16 0.312, int8 0.310 -> small, not explaining full drop.
ci-bot: deploy-check: rerank-eval job 6755554321 completed in 22m, artifacts at s3://redwood-evals/6755554321/
alex: thanks. Next steps proposal:
- compute per-query delta (old_holdout vs relabel_holdout) and rank the worst 200 queries
- inspect whether candidate ordering changed or candidates were truncated/merged
- run tokenizer parity check between offline relabeler and prod tokenizer (same vocab/settings)
- if formatting causes signal loss, revert that specific transform and rerun relabel on a small sample
marta: I'll produce per-query delta CSV and upload to that s3 path by EOD.
devon: ping me when uploaded. I'll run the worst-200 triage and sample human checks (5-10) to see annotation drift. :eyes:
sasha: also consider adding a short eval where we re-insert punctuation only for the last 32 tokens of each candidate — quick experiment to see if tail signal matters.
alex: good idea. keep logs short and snapshots of tokenized sequences for the top mismatches so we can rule out tokenizer mismatch vs true label changes.
marta: uploaded artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/6755554321/deltas.csv and tokenized_samples/
devon: grabbing them now. starting worst-200 pass. will post findings in this thread.
sasha: thanks all — feels like a small pipeline change caused a nontrivial metric shift. if human triage shows labels are stable we should revert formatting until we can do a full parity relabel run.
alex: agree. prioritize a reproducible test harness for relabel transforms (unit test + small eval) before rolling to full dataset.
marta: noted. will open a PR with a revert patch and the parity unit tests.
ci-bot: PR 4821 opened by marta: "relabel: revert punctuation strip; add tokenizer parity tests"
devon: nice, assigning review.
marta: thanks — will follow up with triage notes. :+1:
